::: {.page-intro}
Each workshop opens with a real business question, a naive first answer, why that answer fails, and the method that actually answers it. This page lists the topics covered each week — for the schedule, readings, and assessment details, your [Canvas module](https://canvas.ljmu.ac.uk/courses/126948) is the hub.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

weeks = [
    {"n": 1, "title": "Distributions and Summarising Data",
     "question": "What does our own reaction-time data actually look like?",
     "points": [
         "Exploratory data analysis, and why it comes first",
         "Variable types, tidy data",
         "Histograms, shape, and outliers",
         "Mean, median, variance, standard deviation, IQR",
         "Box plots and violin plots",
         "Comparing two groups — is a difference real?",
     ]},
    {"n": 2, "title": "Inference",
     "question": "Can we trust a number computed from a sample?",
     "points": [
         "External validity — three threats",
         "The sampling distribution and standard error",
         "Unbiasedness, asymptotic normality, root-n convergence",
         "The bootstrap",
         "Confidence intervals",
         "Hypothesis testing, the t-test, and p-values",
     ]},
    {"n": 3, "title": "Relationships Between Variables",
     "question": "Does x actually relate to y — and how would we know?",
     "points": [
         "Conditional probability and the conditional mean",
         "Bin-scatter and stacked bar charts",
         "Covariance and correlation",
         "Spurious correlation",
         "Latent variables — one proxy, z-score averaging, PCA",
     ]},
    {"n": 4, "title": "Regression I — Fitting the Line",
     "question": "How do we turn “y varies with x” into a precise formula?",
     "points": [
         "From LOWESS to a straight line",
         "The OLS estimator — slope and intercept formulas",
         "Why OLS is BLUE, and what that requires",
         "Fitted values and residuals",
         "R² and goodness of fit",
         "Functional form and influential observations",
     ]},
    {"n": 5, "title": "Regression I — Model Problems & Inference",
     "question": "When can we trust the regression line we just fitted?",
     "points": [
         "Choosing functional form — logs, ratios, polynomials",
         "Extreme values vs. influential observations",
         "Measurement error and attenuation bias",
         "Standard errors and confidence intervals for β̂",
         "Homoskedasticity and robust SE",
         "Confidence intervals vs. prediction intervals",
     ]},
    {"n": 6, "title": "Regression II — Multiple Regression",
     "question": "Is x really driving y, or is something else doing the work?",
     "points": [
         "Omitted variable bias vs. multicollinearity",
         "Variance inflation factor (VIF)",
         "Testing several coefficients together — the F-test",
         "Categorical variables and dummy coding",
         "Interactions — different slopes for different groups",
         "Overfitting and variable selection",
     ]},
    {"n": 7, "note": "Curriculum Enrichment Week — no workshop"},
    {"n": 8, "title": "Other Models (GLMs)",
     "question": "Does smoking pose a health risk — for a yes/no outcome?",
     "points": [
         "Binary outcomes and the latent-variable model",
         "The Generalized Linear Model family",
         "Linear probability model, logit, and probit",
         "Marginal effects (AMEs)",
         "Goodness of fit — pseudo-R², Brier score, calibration",
     ]},
    {"n": 9, "title": "Causal Analysis and Experiments",
     "question": "Does working from home change who quits?",
     "points": [
         "Potential outcomes and treatment effects",
         "DAGs — confounders vs. mediators",
         "Why random assignment works",
         "Designing and running an A/B test, power and sample size",
         "Covariate balance",
         "ITT vs. treatment effect, internal and external validity",
     ]},
    {"n": 10, "title": "Prediction",
     "question": "What price should go in the ad?",
     "points": [
         "Loss functions and the bias–variance trade-off",
         "Overfitting, and how we'd actually know",
         "BIC / AIC",
         "Train/test splits and k-fold cross-validation",
         "LASSO",
     ]},
    {"n": 11, "title": "Time Series",
     "question": "How risky is Microsoft stock?",
     "points": [
         "Trend, seasonality, stationarity",
         "Random walks",
         "Spurious regression and differencing",
         "Serial correlation, and why it breaks standard errors",
         "Lagged effects and forecasting",
     ]},
    {"n": 12, "note": "Assessment review and portfolio presentations — see Canvas"},
]

def topic_block(w):
    # Single line per element — Pandoc's raw-HTML-block passthrough is
    # unreliable across multi-line nested tags under `output: asis`.
    if "note" in w:
        return (f'<div class="topic-block is-note">'
                 f'<div class="topic-head"><span class="week-num">Week {w["n"]:02d}</span></div>'
                 f'<p class="note-text">{w["note"]}</p></div>')

    points = "".join(f'<li>{p}</li>' for p in w["points"])
    return (f'<div class="topic-block">'
             f'<div class="topic-head"><span class="week-num">Week {w["n"]:02d}</span>'
             f'<span class="topic-title">{w["title"]}</span></div>'
             f'<p class="topic-question">{w["question"]}</p>'
             f'<ul class="topic-points">{points}</ul></div>')

print('<div class="topics-list">')
for w in weeks:
    print(topic_block(w))
print('</div>')
```
